theory.intro: To estimate a product, round each factor to $1$ significant figure, then multiply the rounded numbers. A one-digit whole-number factor remains unchanged. The estimate is an approximate answer.
facts: To round to $1$ significant figure, find the first non-zero digit and round to its place value. If the next digit is $5$ or more, round up.
$9\times46\approx9\times50=450$. When both factors need rounding, round both: $43\times68\approx40\times70=2800$.
steps: Round each factor to $1$ significant figure. A one-digit whole-number factor remains unchanged.
Use $\approx$ to show that the answer is an estimate.

workedExamples.question_text:
Estimate:
(a) $8\times57$ by rounding $57$ to the nearest $10$
(b) $6\times453$ by rounding $453$ to the nearest $100$
(c) $7\times250$ by rounding $250$ to the nearest $100$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Keep the one-digit factor unchanged.
(a) $57$ rounds to $60$.
$8\times57\approx8\times60=480$
(b) $453$ is nearer to $500$ than $400$.
$6\times453\approx6\times500=3000$
(c) $250$ is halfway between $200$ and $300$. Round up to $300$.
$7\times250\approx7\times300=2100$
